title: I2C (Inter-Integrated Circuit) protocol
summary: I2C is a two-wire serial bus (SDA data, SCL clock) for connecting low-speed peripherals. Communication: START condition (SDA high->low while SCL high), 7-bit (or 10-bit) address + R/W bit, ACK/NACK, data bytes, STOP condition (SDA low->high while SCL high). Clock stretching allows slaves to slow down the master.

ext.summary: I2C is a two-wire serial bus (SDA data, SCL clock) for connecting low-speed peripherals. Communication: START condition (SDA high->low while SCL high), 7-bit (or 10-bit) address + R/W bit, ACK/NACK, data bytes, STOP condition (SDA low->high while SCL high). Clock stretching allows slaves to slow down the master.

structure.meaning: SDA transitions high->low while SCL is high. Signals the beginning of a transaction.
Receiver pulls SDA low during the 9th clock pulse to acknowledge.
Receiver leaves SDA high during the 9th clock pulse (no device at address, or end of read).
Data byte, MSB first. Followed by ACK/NACK.
SDA transitions low->high while SCL is high. Signals the end of a transaction.
START without a preceding STOP. Used to change direction (write then read) without releasing the bus.
10-bit addressing: first byte = 11110XX0 (where XX are the top 2 bits of the address), then the low 8 bits.

notes: I2C uses two wires: SDA (data) and SCL (clock).
Standard mode: 100 kbps. Fast mode: 400 kbps. Fast mode plus: 1 Mbps. High speed: 3.4 Mbps. Ultra fast: 5 Mbps.
I2C supports multi-master and multi-slave configurations.
Clock stretching: slave holds SCL low to slow down the master.
I2C is used for sensors, EEPROMs, RTCs, and many low-speed peripherals.
